name: resource-bulk-fanin
description: resource-bulk's 64 MiB whole-transfer mechanism driven by initiator_count independent sender processes into ONE receiver - the many-links-bulk-receive shape that neither resource-bulk (one sender) nor resource-fanout (many links, 20-120 KB round-trip-bound transfers) exercises. Each sender is its own process with its own reactor, so the send side scales with senders and the receiver is the only shared stage: every arriving segment must be decrypted and hash-proved by the one receiving node. That makes this the scenario that decides whether receive-side decrypt is a per-node serial bottleneck (aggregate goodput flat at the single-link rate no matter how many senders) or scales past one core. run_dakka.sh drives it at any sender count (MANIFEST=scenarios/resource-bulk-fanin/manifest.json ./run_dakka.sh self self N), and its discipline applies: senders and receiver pinned to disjoint core sets, so the saturation curve belongs to the receiver, not the machine.
conformance: Per sender: sent == settled + failures with zero failures for a Prns pair, every segment hash-proved before the next. Responder: received counts whole assembled transfers and payload_bytes covers every settled sender's bytes. The responder announces until initiator_count links are up and reports only after that many close. The request-fanin listener law applies here too: Prns's TcpServerInterface is point-to-point, so the responder binds one listener per sender (READY addr joined by +) and the runner deals each sender its own port.
caveats: Aggregate goodput on a shared-memory loopback rig is an upper-bound shape, not a wire number: all senders and the receiver share one machine's memory bandwidth, so the honest reading is BASE vs candidate on identical placement, and the single-link resource-bulk rate is the per-sender sanity floor.
